issues.name: Agent-friendly 404s
issues.details: Nonexistent paths return HTTP 200 with the app shell (soft-404). Agents probing for resources conclude every path exists. Return a real HTTP 404 status for unknown paths.
issues.recommendation: Return a real HTTP 404 (or 410) status for nonexistent paths - never a 200 with your app shell, which makes agents believe every path exists. For full credit, give the 404 response a short markdown body pointing agents at your sitemap, llms.txt, or docs index. Verify with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://yourdomain.com/some-path-that-does-not-exist` - it must print 404.

issues.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
issues.details: No agent instruction file with when-to-use guidance found
issues.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

issues.name: Rate limit response headers
issues.details: No REST rate-limit headers found on probed endpoints
issues.recommendation: Return standard rate-limit headers on your API responses (the RFC RateLimit headers, plus Retry-After on a 429) so agents can self-throttle in real time, and document the conventions alongside your API.

issues.name: MCP server / manifest
issues.details: MCP server live at /mcp but initialize requires authentication (HTTP 307 redirect).
issues.recommendation: Build an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing your API as tools. Use Streamable HTTP transport for full score. This lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI agents call your product natively.

roster.name: Code fence validity
roster.details: Code fences balanced in served markdown.
roster.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.

roster.name: OpenAPI spec published
roster.details: OpenAPI spec found at /openapi.json and parses with a paths object.
roster.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

roster.name: Scoped permissions
roster.details: Scoped permissions defined and enforced per-operation.
roster.recommendation: Declare scoped API permissions where machines can read them: named OAuth scopes in your OpenAPI security schemes, or scopes_supported in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata. Prose descriptions of roles help humans, but agents need the machine-readable declaration to request least-privilege access.

roster.name: Agent crawler reachability
roster.details: All probed AI crawlers reach the homepage.
roster.recommendation: Allowlist the major AI crawler/agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, ora-agent, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF, bot-detection rules, and robots.txt so agents can reach your homepage.

roster.name: Not blocked by bot detection
roster.details: No bot-detection challenge for agent traffic.
roster.recommendation: Allowlist known AI agent User-Agents (ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot) in your WAF or bot-detection rules.

roster.name: JSON error responses
roster.details: API returns JSON error responses with error details.
roster.recommendation: Return structured JSON error responses with error codes, messages, and resolution hints. Agents can't parse HTML error pages.

roster.name: OAuth 2.0 support
roster.details: oauth-authorization-server metadata responds with JSON at .well-known.
roster.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 for API authentication. Publish your authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

roster.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
roster.details: Public API documentation served at /docs/api.
roster.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.

roster.name: Developer portal
roster.details: Developer portal present (/integrations, /docs) with quickstart/key guidance.
roster.recommendation: Create a developer portal at /developers with API keys, documentation, quickstart guides, and a sandbox environment.

roster.name: Public API with reachable endpoints
roster.details: Public API reachable and referenced across the site.
roster.recommendation: Expose a public REST or GraphQL API. AI agents need programmatic access  - not just a web UI  - to integrate with your product.

roster.name: API schema complexity analysis
roster.details: Spec carries a reusable component/definition schema section.
roster.recommendation: Make your API spec self-describing: a unique operationId and a description on every operation, typed parameters, and response schemas. For GraphQL, a fully typed schema with a documented cost or rate limit reads best.

roster.name: Function calling compatibility
roster.details: 393 operations, 98% with summaries/descriptions — LLM function-calling ready.
roster.recommendation: Ensure API endpoints have unique operation IDs, typed schemas, and descriptions compatible with LLM function-calling formats.

roster.name: Sandbox / test environment
roster.details: Sandbox / test-mode environment documented.
roster.recommendation: Provide a sandbox or test mode so agents can exercise your API without touching production data, and document how to reach it - this lowers the risk of a destructive call against live data.

roster.name: REST response schema coverage
roster.details: Response schema coverage ~100%.
roster.recommendation: Define typed JSON response schemas for every endpoint in your OpenAPI spec. Agents rely on these to know what fields they will get back; missing or partial schemas force trial-and-error.

roster.name: CLI tool available
roster.details: Published CLI package found on npm with a bin entry.
roster.recommendation: Publish an official CLI tool on npm, PyPI, or Homebrew. A CLI lets agents and developers script interactions with your product without building API integrations from scratch.

roster.name: REST typed error model
roster.details: Typed error responses documented across the API surface.
roster.recommendation: Document your error responses in your OpenAPI spec: give 4xx and 5xx responses a typed error schema (or use RFC 9457 application/problem+json). A consistent error object with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message lets agents handle failures without guessing.

roster.name: REST versioning / deprecation policy
roster.details: API versioning policy evident in spec paths/info.
roster.recommendation: Declare a versioning policy agents can rely on: version your API (in the URL path or a version header) and publish how you signal deprecation (a Sunset/Deprecation header or a documented timeline). Agents avoid integrating against a surface that can change without warning.

roster.name: REST pagination pattern
roster.details: Pagination parameters documented in list endpoints.
roster.recommendation: Use a consistent, documented pagination shape on your list endpoints (cursor-based preferred) and define the pagination fields in your OpenAPI response schemas, so agents can page through results without guessing the shape.

roster.name: Multi-language SDK packages
roster.details: Official SDKs published to npm and PyPI.
roster.recommendation: Publish official SDK packages across multiple language ecosystems (npm, PyPI, Go modules, RubyGems). Auto-generate them from your OpenAPI spec using tools like openapi-generator. For each package set the project URL or homepage to your product domain (package.json `repository`/`homepage`, PyPI `Home-Page` or `project_urls`, RubyGems `homepage_uri`) - this is how agents verify the package is your official SDK.

roster.name: Redirect hygiene
roster.details: Already served over HTTPS.
roster.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

roster.name: Metadata completeness
roster.details: 6 of 6 metadata signals present (title, description, canonical, OG, Twitter).
roster.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical">, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

roster.name: JSON-LD structured data
roster.details: Valid JSON-LD identity node (Organization) with name and url.
roster.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

roster.name: JSON-LD entity linking (sameAs)
roster.details: sameAs links connect the identity entity to external references.
roster.recommendation: Add sameAs links in your JSON-LD structured data pointing to your Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry, GitHub org, and social profiles. This helps AI disambiguate your brand from similarly named entities.

roster.name: Organization schema completeness
roster.details: Organization schema includes contactPoint and address.
roster.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

roster.name: Trust anchor pages
roster.details: About, Contact and Privacy anchors all resolve.
roster.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

roster.name: Content behind auth
roster.details: Documentation paths serve content without authentication.
roster.recommendation: Serve your content pages without a login wall. Agents cannot complete auth flows while browsing - a 401/403 or a login-form page is invisible content. Keep public documentation public; if some content must stay gated, publish an ungated summary so agents can still represent it.

roster.name: Page token budget
roster.details: Homepage fits agent context budgets (~700 tokens).
roster.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

roster.name: Content without JavaScript
roster.details: Server HTML carries 3631 chars of readable copy with an H1 heading.
roster.recommendation: Server-side render your homepage so AI crawlers see meaningful content without JavaScript. Ensure an H1 and 500+ chars of text in raw HTML.

roster.name: llms.txt exists
roster.details: /llms.txt is published.
roster.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

roster.name: llms.txt formatting
roster.details: /llms.txt has an H1 and 18 markdown links.
roster.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

roster.name: Sitemap exists
roster.details: Valid XML sitemap with 6372 URL entries.
roster.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

roster.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
roster.details: Sitemap includes <lastmod> freshness signals.
roster.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

roster.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
roster.details: Canonical URL serves text/markdown and text/html via Accept negotiation with Vary: Accept
roster.recommendation: On the responses that serve text/markdown via Accept negotiation, add Accept to the Vary header (Vary: Accept, Accept-Encoding). Without it, CDNs can serve the cached HTML variant to an agent asking for markdown (or vice versa), depending on which variant landed in cache first.

roster.name: MCP server / manifest
roster.details: MCP server live at /mcp but initialize requires authentication (HTTP 307 redirect).
roster.recommendation: Build an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing your API as tools. Use Streamable HTTP transport for full score. This lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI agents call your product natively.

roster.name: REST async-job pattern
roster.details: 202 response documented but no status-endpoint contract.
roster.recommendation: For long-running operations, return 202 Accepted and point agents at where to poll for the result (a status/location reference plus a job identifier in the body), documented in your OpenAPI spec, so work that does not finish in one request is still followable.

roster.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
roster.details: robots.txt exists but has no AI-agent-specific user-agent rules (falls back to *).
roster.recommendation: Stop blocking user-triggered agents in robots.txt. Remove any 'Disallow: /' that applies to ChatGPT-User, Claude-User or Perplexity-User - including a blanket 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', which covers them by default. These agents fetch a page only because a person just asked about you, so a block turns away your highest-intent traffic.

roster.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
roster.details: Fewer than 2 agent-specific rule groups; policy granularity is low.
roster.recommendation: Add explicit AI crawler directives in robots.txt. Allow the crawlers that feed answer engines ('User-agent: GPTBot' / 'Allow: /', same for ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot), and restrict training-only crawlers (CCBot, ByteSpider) with 'Disallow: /'. Content Signals ('Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no') earns the same credit.

roster.name: MCP well-known discovery
roster.details: Live MCP server but no discovery manifest at .well-known paths.
roster.recommendation: Serve your MCP server at /.well-known/mcp, publish a server-card.json at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, or reference it in llms.txt so agents can discover it automatically without manual URL input.

This lets agents pay on behalf of users with scoped, revocable credentials.
